linh: Hey team — first week, mostly set up but running into an annoying asdf/shims vs system PATH issue. `which python` points to /usr/bin/python while `asdf current python` shows 3.11. Getting wheel/build failures when installing deps in project. Also poetry seems to be using the system site packages. Anyone seen this shim ordering weirdness on macos arm?
omar: Welcome! Most likely your shell init order is wrong. Key points: 1) asdf shims should be early on PATH, 2) asdf init should run in interactive login shells, and 3) Homebrew/opt paths must be exported before building python. For zsh add to ~/.zprofile (login) or ~/.zshenv (non-interactive) depending on how you start sessions. Example minimal bits:

export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
eval "$(asdf init -)"

Make sure you don't clobber PATH later in .zshrc or dotfiles.
sasha: Another gotcha: GUI apps (VSCode launched from Finder) don't read .zprofile/.zshrc. If you open VSCode from the Dock, it may get a different PATH. Launch VSCode from the terminal (`code .`) after your shell is fixed or add a plist to export PATH for GUI apps.

rebecca: For poetry specifically, check `poetry env info` and `poetry env use $(which python)`. If Poetry created a virtualenv with the system python you can recreate it: `poetry env remove python` then `poetry env use 3.11` (after asdf points to the right python). Also run `asdf reshim python` after installs.

linh: I did `eval "$(asdf init -)"` in .zshrc, but which python still shows /usr/bin/python. I think dotfiles are overwriting PATH later. How to debug?
omar: Put `echo PATH_BEFORE:$PATH` at top and `echo PATH_AFTER:$PATH` at bottom of your zsh files to see where it's changed. Or run `env | rg ASDF -n` and `type -a python` to list all python binaries. Typical culprits: dotfiles that re-add Homebrew later, or a ~/.profile from previous setups.

sasha: If using launchctl/GUI issues, you can add a file to ~/.config/environment.d/ to set PATH system-wide on mac (or use launchctl setenv on older macOS). But usually simpler: start VSCode from terminal for dev work.

rebecca: Also check if pipx/poetry installed a shim under /usr/local/bin that wins. `ls -l $(which python)` and `ls -l $(which poetry)` helps. Remove old shims (or reorder PATH).

linh: Good tips — I discovered my dotfiles included a line that re-sourced an old .profile which reset PATH. Removed it and now `which python` points to ~/.asdf/shims/python. Poetry still used the old env though. I followed `poetry env use 3.11` and recreated venv, good now.

omar: Nice. Couple of extra bits for Mac/arm: make sure Homebrew libs are available for building wheels:

export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib -L/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include -I/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig:/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/lib/pkgconfig"

and then rebuild the env.

rebecca: Tiny note: after changing PATH you may have to `rehash` or `exec $SHELL` to clear old cached locations.

linh: One last friction: our repo has a pre-commit hook that assumes `python` is the project python. After fix, pre-commit passes. I'll open a small PR to dotfiles to document the recommended asdf-first ordering and mention VSCode-from-finder caveat.
dotfiles-bot: Please include the snippet template (dotfiles/macos/asdf-path-order.md) and add a changelog entry.

infra-bot: Reminder: new-hires should verify "dev-tooling" on the onboarding checklist (https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboard). Mark step 3 when finished.

linh: Thanks everyone! Saved me a lot of head-scratching — PR incoming in a few minutes. :)

omar: Welcome aboard :wave: ping if you want a quick pairing to check your dotfiles.
